summary: First checkpoint of Profinite and pro-p groups, Part II: p-adic measures and Iwasawa algebras. Decomposes the algebraic carrier, integral inclusion, cleared numerators and admissible evaluation of L3 pseudomeasures. The generic coefficient ring, total quotient ring and Dirac homomorphism are explicit data; identifying them with completed group algebras and continuous-character integration remains open. All eight layers remain in scope. No layer is claimed closed.

nodes.title: Pseudomeasures
nodes.statement: Define Iwasawa.pseudomeasures δ Q : Submodule R Q to be (1 : Submodule R Q) / Submodule.span R (range (g ↦ ι(δ(g)−1))). This uses the existing submodule quotient. It is an R-module; it is not asserted to be a subring, a fractional ideal in the domain-specific sense, or a topological completion.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: Use the existing total quotient ring and Submodule.div. The unit submodule is the image of R by Submodule.one_eq_range.
Take the span of the Dirac differences and the quotient of the unit submodule by that span. All additive and R-module structure is inherited.
Subtype extensionality is routine. If δ(g)=1 for every g, the span is zero and the defining membership condition holds for every q ∈ Q.

nodes.title: Integrality by Dirac differences
nodes.statement: For z ∈ Q, z ∈ pseudomeasures δ Q iff ∀ g : G, ∃ r : R, ι(r)=ι(c_g)z.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: Unfold the carrier and apply Submodule.mem_div_iff_forall_mul_mem.
The forward implication tests each generator of the span and uses Submodule.mem_one.
Conversely use Submodule.span_induction: integrality is preserved by zero, addition and R-scalar multiplication. Commutativity exchanges zι(c_g) with ι(c_g)z.
acceptance: For δ=Units.coeHom ℤ, the generator g=−1 requires −2z ∈ ℤ, whereas g=1 gives no condition. Thus z=1/2 passes and z=1/4 fails.

nodes.title: Integral inclusion
nodes.statement: Define Iwasawa.integral δ Q : R →ₗ[R] pseudomeasures δ Q by r ↦ ι(r).
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: For every g, ι(c_g)ι(r)=ι(c_g r), so the membership lemma applies.
Restrict the codomain of the scalar linear map to the pseudomeasure submodule. The ring-map laws give linearity.
Injectivity is inherited from IsFractionRing.injective.

nodes.title: Cleared numerator
nodes.statement: For g ∈ G define Iwasawa.numerator δ Q g : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] R by the unique n_g(z) satisfying ι(n_g(z))=ι(c_g)z.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: Existence is exactly pseudomeasure-membership. Uniqueness follows from IsFractionRing.injective.
Choose the unique preimage. Apply injectivity to prove addition and scalar multiplication laws using the defining equality; this yields one R-linear map.
For integral r its numerator is c_g r, by integral-inclusion-value. For g=1 the factor vanishes and injectivity forces numerator zero.

nodes.statement: For every g and pseudomeasure z, ι(numerator δ Q g z)=ι(c_g)z.

acceptance: For R=ℤ, Q=ℚ, δ=Units.coeHom ℤ, g=−1 and z=1/2, the equality reads ι(−1)=ι(−2)(1/2). The opposite sign for the numerator fails this check.

nodes.title: Commuting cleared numerators
nodes.statement: For g,h ∈ G and a pseudomeasure z, c_h n_g(z)=c_g n_h(z) in R.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: Apply IsFractionRing.injective.
Map both sides to Q and replace the two numerators by cleared-numerator-spec. Commutativity and associativity identify both products with ι(c_h)ι(c_g)z.
acceptance: Taking g=1 forces both sides to zero, using n_1=0; taking g=h gives the reflexive identity. For two admissible factors the identity must survive every coefficient homomorphism.

nodes.title: Admissible pseudomeasure evaluation
nodes.statement: For g ∈ G with hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)), define Iwasawa.evalAt δ Q A g hg : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] A by z ↦ u⁻¹ f(n_g(z)), where u is the unit represented by hg. The requirement is a unit in A, not merely a nonzero element.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)).
proofSteps: Compose the numerator R-linear map with the scalar map R → A.
Multiply by the inverse of the unit supplied by hg. Since A is commutative this multiplication is R-linear.
The inverse-unit identities establish the evaluation equation. No map Q → A is assumed or constructed.

nodes.title: Evaluation equation
nodes.statement: For an admissible g and every pseudomeasure z, f(c_g) evalAt_g(z)=f(n_g(z)).
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.

hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)).
proofSteps: Unfold evaluation and cancel the unit with its chosen inverse.

nodes.title: Independence of clearing factor
nodes.statement: If f(c_g) and f(c_h) are units, evalAt δ Q A g hg = evalAt δ Q A h hh as R-linear maps.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)); hh : IsUnit (f(c_h)).
proofSteps: Apply f to cross-multiplied-numerators.
Substitute the two evaluation equations. Commutativity gives f(c_h)f(c_g)evalAt_g(z)=f(c_h)f(c_g)evalAt_h(z).
Cancel the two units with IsUnit.mul_left_cancel. Extensionality of linear maps gives the result. This also removes any dependence on the witness of IsUnit.
acceptance: With g=h the result identifies any two witnesses of the same IsUnit condition. With distinct g,h the proof must use the cross-numerator relation and cancellation of units, and must not assume a ring homomorphism from Q to A.

nodes.title: Evaluation of integral measures
nodes.statement: For every r ∈ R and admissible g, evalAt_g(integral r)=f(r).
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)).
proofSteps: Map the numerator specification for integral r to Q and use integral-inclusion-value; injectivity identifies the numerator with c_g r.
Use the evaluation equation and cancel f(c_g) with IsUnit.mul_left_cancel.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of admissible evaluation
nodes.statement: Let g be admissible. If L : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] A satisfies L(integral r)=f(r) for every r, then L=evalAt_g.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)); L is R-linear and extends f on the integral inclusion.
proofSteps: For each z, prove c_g • z = integral(n_g(z)) by subtype extensionality, integral-inclusion-value and cleared-numerator-spec.
Apply L and use R-linearity and the extension condition to obtain f(c_g)L(z)=f(n_g(z)).
Compare with admissible-evaluation-spec and cancel the unit.
acceptance: For R=ℤ, Q=A=ℚ and δ=Units.coeHom ℤ, every ℤ-linear extension of integer inclusion must send 1/2 to 1/2, since doubling that element gives integral 1. No multiplicative structure on the pseudomeasure carrier is assumed.

sources.locator: Equation (3-11) and Remark 3.35, printed p. 130 / PDF 31
sources.match: This is the corrected uniqueness statement for a linear extension on pseudomeasures. It does not assert a ring homomorphism on all of Q(G). The formulation over an explicit δ into an arbitrary commutative ring is a worker generalization of the source argument; the paper specializes to completed group algebras.

nodes.title: Evaluation under coefficient change
nodes.statement: Let k : A →ₐ[R] B with B a commutative R-algebra. For g admissible in A and in B, k(evalAt_g^A(z))=evalAt_g^B(z). The second admissibility follows automatically from IsUnit.map and the algebra-map compatibility of k.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
B is a commutative R-algebra; k : A →ₐ[R] B; g has unit factor in A (hence also in B).
proofSteps: Map the evaluation equation from A to B using k.
The R-algebra law identifies k(f_A(c_g)) with f_B(c_g), and likewise for n_g(z).
Compare with the evaluation equation in B and cancel its unit. Identity and composition compatibility follow by specializing k and evaluating composed functions.
acceptance: For k=id_A the equality is reflexive; applying it successively along A→B→C gives the same equality as the composite. In particular it transports the rational value 1/2 along ℚ→ℝ in the integer-units example.

nodes.title: Obstruction to total quotient evaluation
nodes.statement: Let f : R →+* A with A a nontrivial commutative ring. If s ∈ nonZeroDivisors R and f(s)=0, there is no F : Q →+* A with F.comp (algebraMap R Q)=f.
hypotheses: R,Q are commutative rings, Q is an R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q.
A is a nontrivial commutative ring; f : R →+* A; s is a non-zero-divisor of R killed by f.
proofSteps: IsLocalization.map_units makes ι(s) a unit in Q.
If F existed, IsUnit.map would make F(ι(s))=f(s)=0 a unit in A, contradicting not_isUnit_zero.
The existing IsLocalization.lift has the stronger denominator hypothesis needed to extend a map on all of Q. It supplies no such lift merely because f is a character integral.
acceptance: For R=ℚ[X], evaluation at 0 kills the regular element X, so it cannot extend to FractionRing R.
For R=ℚ[X], evaluation at 3 kills the regular element X−3; nonzero evaluation points do not resolve the obstruction.
The condition that 2 ≠ 0 in ℤ does not make 2 invertible; general-target evaluation must require IsUnit.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 3.35, published printed p. 130 / PDF 31; same assertion in arXiv v2 PDF 22.
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims there is exactly one homomorphism Q(G) → C_p.
sourceIssues.correction: A continuous character integral extends to a localization only when every inverted element has unit image. A pseudomeasure can instead be evaluated by (3-11) once one Dirac difference has nonzero character value. It does not generally extend to all of Q(G).
sourceIssues.reason: Take p=3, G=ℤ₃ with generator γ, and R=ℤ₃[[T]] with [γ]=1+T. The continuous nontrivial character χ(x)=4^x gives the convergent evaluation T↦3. The nonzero regular series T−3 maps to zero, so no extension to Q(R) exists: its inverse would force 0=1. This example meets the remark’s nontrivial-character hypothesis. Separately, augmentation T↦0 kills T. The generic obstruction node and the two polynomial test cases isolate the same algebraic failure. Accepted RS-16 already warns against whole-fraction augmentation; no published erratum was found in the listed search.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.36(iii), published printed p. 131 / PDF 32; arXiv v2 PDF 23.
sourceIssues.printed: The proof imposes the condition a ≠ 1.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose an integer a>1 prime to p, for example p+1; more generally choose a of infinite order, so a^k−1≠0 for every positive k.
sourceIssues.reason: The stated choice of an integer a≠1 prime to p allows a=−1. Its even moments vanish, so [a]−[1] does not satisfy part (ii), contrary to the proof’s next claim. Indeed ([−1]−[1])([−1]+[1])=0. The two factors are nonzero for the characteristic-zero coefficient ring, as seen in a finite quotient distinguishing ±1. Taking a=p+1 repairs this step and leaves the lemma intact.
